  first paint and appears after hydration. (Also good for LCP; the PDP rail is inside

128	import { ZimmRecentlyViewedRail } from '../ui-kits/organisms/zimmRecentlyViewedRail';
129	import type { ZimmProductCardProps } from '../ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard';
130	import { selectRecentlyViewedCard } from '../../utils/recentlyViewedCard';
131	import type { RecentlyViewedCard } from '../../utils/recentlyViewedCard';
132	import { useRecentlyViewedHistory } from '../../hooks/useRecentlyViewedHistory';
133	import { useRecentlyViewedProductFetch } from '../../utils/recentlyViewedProductFetch';
134	
135	/**
136	 * The one field this file reads off a recommendation-context product. A real
137	 * commerce-sdk-isomorphic Product shape underlies it, but @salesforce/retail-react-app's
138	 * useEinstein/ProductScroller ship untyped (vendor.d.ts's wildcard), so this is narrowed
139	 * to exactly the field touched here rather than invented more broadly (AGENTS.md > Type
140	 * Definitions: hand-roll only the genuinely unexported shape actually used).
141	 */
142	type RecommendedProduct = { productId?: string };
143	
144	/**
145	 * Stable empty-id-list reference passed to `useRecentlyViewedProductFetch` for every recommender
146	 * except Recently-Viewed itself (see the hook call below) — an inline `[]` literal would behave
147	 * identically (`cappedIds.length > 0` is `false` either way, per
148	 * recentlyViewedProductFetch.ts's own `enabled` check), but a module-level constant avoids
149	 * allocating a fresh array on every render for no reason. Same naming/intent as
150	 * `useRecentlyViewedHistory.ts`'s own `EMPTY_IDS`
151	 * (overrides/app/hooks/useRecentlyViewedHistory.ts:18).
152	 */
153	const NO_RECENTLY_VIEWED_IDS: readonly string[] = [];
154	
155	export type RecommendedProductsProps = {
156	  /* The title to appear above the product scroller */
157	  title?: ReactNode;
158	
159	  /* The zone to request */
160	  zone?: string;
161	
162	  /* The recommender to request */
163	  recommender?: string;
164	
165	  /* The products to use for recommendation context */
166	  products?: readonly Record<string, unknown>[];
167	
168	  /* Callback to determine if the component should fetch results */
169	  shouldFetch?: () => boolean;
170	
171	  // Index signature for the `...props` passthrough to ProductScroller (itself untyped — see
172	  // vendor.d.ts). Without it, the destructured rest types as `{}` instead of accepting arbitrary
173	  // passthrough, which is the base file's actual intent: forwarding whatever else the caller
174	  // passes.
175	  [key: string]: unknown;
176	};
177	
178	/**
179	 * A component for fetching and rendering product recommendations from the Einstein API
180	 * by a zone or a recommender name.
181	 */
182	const RecommendedProducts = ({
183	  zone,
184	  recommender,
185	  products,
186	  title,
187	  shouldFetch,
188	  ...props
189	}: RecommendedProductsProps) => {
190	  const { isLoading, recommendations, getZoneRecommendations, getRecommendations, sendClickReco, sendViewReco } =
191	    useEinstein();
192	  const { data: customer } = useCurrentCustomer();
193	  const { customerId } = customer;
194	  const { data: wishlist } = useWishList();
195	  const dataCloud = useDataCloud();
196	
197	  const createCustomerProductListItem = useShopperCustomersMutation('createCustomerProductListItem');
198	  const deleteCustomerProductListItem = useShopperCustomersMutation('deleteCustomerProductListItem');
199	  const toast = useToast();
200	  const navigate = useNavigation();
201	  const intl = useIntl();
202	  // Same split product-list/productListCardMapper.ts's own consumer uses
203	  // (product-list/index.tsx): passed into the mapper rather than formatted there, keeping that
204	  // mapper free of any react-intl dependency of its own.
205	  const formatPrice = (amount: number, currency: string) => intl.formatNumber(amount, { style: 'currency', currency });
206	
207	  const ref = useRef();
208	  const isOnScreen = useIntersectionObserver(ref, { useOnce: true });
209	  const [_products, setProducts] = useState(products);
210	  // Unconditional, alongside the hook calls above — must run on every render, including the
211	  // ones that hit the dead-code early returns further below, per React's rules of hooks.
212	  const { hasRecentlyViewed, recentlyViewedIds } = useRecentlyViewedHistory();
213	  // Also unconditional, same rules-of-hooks reason — but only ever given this shopper's real
214	  // tracked ids (and therefore only ever allowed to fire its own `getProducts` request, per its
215	  // own `enabled: cappedIds.length > 0`) when this particular instance is actually the
216	  // Recently-Viewed branch below. Every other recommender rendered on the same page (e.g. PDP's
217	  // own Might-Also-Like rail, mounted right alongside this one) would otherwise silently trigger
218	  // a second, unread product fetch whenever this browser already has tracked view history — the
219	  // same "network call fetching data nothing will ever read" problem fixed for
220	  // getRecommendations/getZoneRecommendations below, applied here to the fetch this branch adds.
221	  const { products: recentlyViewedProducts } = useRecentlyViewedProductFetch(
222	    recommender === EINSTEIN_RECOMMENDERS.PDP_RECENTLY_VIEWED ? recentlyViewedIds : NO_RECENTLY_VIEWED_IDS,
223	  );
224	
225	  useEffect(() => {
226	    // SFCC-83/84 build plan A6, bug fix #2 (2026-09-08 revision) — Recently Viewed no longer
227	    // reads Einstein's `recommendations` at all (see the branch further below), so calling
228	    // `getRecommendations`/`getZoneRecommendations` for it would be a real network request
229	    // fetching a response nothing ever reads. Skip both below for this one recommender; every
230	    // other recommender's fetch is unaffected.
231	    if (recommender === EINSTEIN_RECOMMENDERS.PDP_RECENTLY_VIEWED) {
232	      return;
233	    }
234	
235	    // Check if the component should fetch results or not. This is useful
236	    // when you are still waiting on additional data, like `products`.
237	    if (typeof shouldFetch === 'function' && !shouldFetch()) {
238	      return;
239	    }
240	
241	    // Fetch either zone or recommender, but not both. If a zone and recommender
242	    // name are both provided, `zone` takes precendence.
243	    if (zone) {
244	      getZoneRecommendations(zone, _products);
245	      return;
246	    }
247	    if (recommender) {
248	      getRecommendations(recommender, _products);
249	      return;
250	    }
251	  }, [zone, recommender, _products]);
252	
253	  useEffect(() => {
254	    // This is an optimization that eliminates superfluous rerenders/fetching by
255	    // keeping a copy of the `products` array prop in state for shallow comparison.
256	    if (!Array.isArray(products)) {
257	      return;
258	    }
259	    if (products.length !== _products?.length || !products.every((val, index) => val === _products?.[index])) {
260	      setProducts(products);
261	    }
262	  }, [products]);
263	
264	  useEffect(() => {
265	    if (isOnScreen && recommendations?.recs) {
266	      sendViewReco(
267	        {
268	          recommenderName: recommendations.recommenderName,
269	          __recoUUID: recommendations.recoUUID,
270	        },
271	        recommendations.recs.map((rec: { id?: string }) => ({ id: rec.id })),
272	      );
273	      dataCloud.sendViewRecommendations(
274	        {
275	          recommenderName: recommendations.recommenderName,
276	          __recoUUID: recommendations.recoUUID,
277	        },
278	        recommendations.recs.map((rec: { id?: string }) => ({ id: rec.id })),
279	      );
280	    }
281	  }, [isOnScreen, recommendations]);
282	
283	  // SFCC-83 — Recently Viewed only. Every other recommender falls through to the unchanged
284	  // ProductScroller branch below. Moved ahead of the dead-check below (build plan A6, bug fix #3,
285	  // 2026-09-08 revision) — see this file's own module docblock for the full "why". In short: this
286	  // branch's cards no longer come from `recommendations` at all (see the effect above, bug fix
287	  // #2), so `recommendations`/`isLoading` stay at `useEinstein()`'s own untouched initial state
288	  // (`[]`/`false`) for this recommender, which would make the dead-check below evaluate `true`
289	  // unconditionally (via its `recommendations.length < 1` clause specifically, since
290	  // `recommendations` itself stays a truthy `[]`, never falsy) and return `null` regardless of
291	  // `hasRecentlyViewed` if this branch still ran after it. Every other recommender is unaffected
292	  // by the reordering — they still hit the exact same dead-check + ProductScroller path below,
293	  // unchanged, just after this check now short-circuits past them when it applies.
294	  if (recommender === EINSTEIN_RECOMMENDERS.PDP_RECENTLY_VIEWED) {
295	    // AC 8's empty-state gate — see useRecentlyViewedHistory.ts's own docblock. No rail, no
296	    // title, no placeholder.
297	    if (!hasRecentlyViewed) {
298	      return null;
299	    }
300	
301	    // `recentlyViewedProducts` is real, strongly-typed Commerce API data (see
302	    // recentlyViewedProductFetch.ts), unlike the old `recommendations.recs` chain this replaces —
303	    // nothing here is `any`, so (unlike the untouched `.find`/`.some`/`.map` callbacks elsewhere
304	    // in this file, which still read off `useEinstein()`'s untyped `recommendations`) no step of
305	    // this chain needs an explicit parameter-type annotation to satisfy `noImplicitAny`.
306	    const cards: ZimmProductCardProps[] = recentlyViewedProducts
307	      .map((product) => selectRecentlyViewedCard(product, formatPrice))
308	      .filter((card: RecentlyViewedCard | null): card is RecentlyViewedCard => card !== null)
309	      .map(
310	        (card: RecentlyViewedCard): ZimmProductCardProps => ({
311	          ...card,
312	          // Inert for this variation — ZimmProductCardContent never mounts when
313	          // variation: 'recentlyViewed' (zimmProductCard/index.tsx's
314	          // VARIATION_CONFIG.showContent). 'h3' matches the one other established value for
315	          // this same required field (product-list/productListCardMapper.ts).
316	          headingLevel: 'h3',
317	          variation: 'recentlyViewed',
318	        }),
319	      );
320	
321	    return (
322	      // Ref-attachment point — see the module docblock's own isOnScreen/forwardRef note above for
323	      // why this wrapper exists at all. `{...props}` forwards the caller's own layout props (e.g.
324	      // PDP's `mx={{base: -4, md: -8, lg: 0}}`, Cart's `mx={{base: -4, sm: -6, lg: 0}}`) exactly
325	      // as the ProductScroller branch below already does — without it, this branch would render
326	      // inset inside the page's normal content padding while every sibling rail on the same page
327	      // bleeds edge-to-edge, and zimmRecentlyViewedRail.css.ts's own card-width math (e.g.
328	      // 201x2=402) assumes the full viewport width is actually available. `title` is passed
329	      // straight through, no `recommendations?.displayMessage` fallback — `recommendations` is
330	      // never populated for this branch (see above), and this component owns no copy of its own
331	      // (build plan A5/A6): the real title always comes from the caller.
332	      <Box ref={ref} {...(props as BoxProps)}>
333	        <ZimmRecentlyViewedRail title={title} cards={cards} />
334	      </Box>
335	    );
336	  }
337	
338	  // The component should remove itself altogether if it has no recommendations
339	  // and we aren't loading any.
340	  if (!isLoading && (!recommendations || recommendations.length < 1)) {
341	    return null;
342	  }
343	
344	  // TODO: DRY this handler when intl provider is available globally
345	  const addItemToWishlist = async (product: RecommendedProduct) => {
346	    try {
347	      if (!wishlist || !customerId) {
348	        return;
349	      }
350	      await createCustomerProductListItem.mutateAsync({
351	        parameters: {
352	          listId: wishlist.id,
353	          customerId,
354	        },
355	        body: {
356	          quantity: 1,
357	          productId: product.productId,
358	          public: false,
359	          priority: 1,
360	          type: 'product',
361	        },
362	      });
363	
364	      toast({
365	        title: intl.formatMessage(TOAST_MESSAGE_ADDED_TO_WISHLIST, { quantity: 1 }),
366	        status: 'success',
367	        action: (
368	          // it would be better if we could use <Button as={Link}>
369	          // but unfortunately the Link component is not compatible
370	          // with Chakra Toast, since the ToastManager is rendered via portal
371	          // and the toast doesn't have access to intl provider, which is a
372	          // requirement of the Link component.
373	          <Button variant="link" onClick={() => navigate('/account/wishlist')}>
374	            {intl.formatMessage(TOAST_ACTION_VIEW_WISHLIST)}
375	          </Button>
376	        ),
377	      });
378	    } catch {
379	      toast({
380	        title: intl.formatMessage(API_ERROR_MESSAGE),
381	        status: 'error',
382	      });
383	    }
384	  };
385	
386	  const removeItemFromWishlist = async (product: RecommendedProduct) => {
387	    try {
388	      const wishlistItem = wishlist?.customerProductListItems?.find(
389	        (item: { productId?: string }) => item.productId === product.productId,
390	      );
391	      if (!wishlistItem || !wishlist || !customerId) {
392	        return;
393	      }
394	      await deleteCustomerProductListItem.mutateAsync({
395	        parameters: {
396	          customerId,
397	          itemId: wishlistItem.id,
398	          listId: wishlist.id,
399	        },
400	      });
401	      toast({
402	        title: intl.formatMessage(TOAST_MESSAGE_REMOVED_FROM_WISHLIST),
403	        status: 'success',
404	        id: product.productId,
405	      });
406	    } catch {
407	      toast({
408	        title: intl.formatMessage(API_ERROR_MESSAGE),
409	        status: 'error',
410	      });
411	    }
412	  };
413	
414	  return (
415	    <ProductScroller
416	      ref={ref}
417	      title={title || recommendations?.displayMessage}
418	      products={recommendations.recs}
419	      isLoading={isLoading}
420	      productTileProps={(product: RecommendedProduct) => ({
421	        onClick: () => {
422	          sendClickReco(
423	            {
424	              recommenderName: recommendations.recommenderName,
425	              __recoUUID: recommendations.recoUUID,
426	            },
427	            product,
428	          );
429	        },
430	        enableFavourite: true,
431	        isFavourite: wishlist?.customerProductListItems?.some(
432	          (item: { productId?: string }) => item.productId === product?.productId,
433	        ),
434	        onFavouriteToggle: (toBeFavourite: boolean) => {
435	          const action = toBeFavourite ? addItemToWishlist : removeItemFromWishlist;
436	          return action(product);
437	        },
438	      })}
439	      {...props}
440	    />
441	  );
442	};
443	
444	export default RecommendedProducts;

content.text:
All the `findings.md` 🟡 CLARIFY items are either pre-existing planning-stage questions already resolved within the plan.md sections I read (architecture fork, PLP/route ownership, Figma node identification) or orthogonal to this step (cross-device Einstein provisioning). None bear on the two bugs I was directed to fix or on the data-flow rewire itself — those were explicit, direct instructions in my task, independently verified against `use-einstein.js`'s real source rather than taken on faith.

## Summary

**Branch:** `feature/SFCC-83-84_recently-viewed` (confirmed not `develop`/`main` before starting).

### Files changed (exactly the two named, nothing else)

**`/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/components/recommended-products/index.tsx`**

1. **Import/hook rename** (line ~105, ~173): `useRecentlyViewedGate` → `useRecentlyViewedHistory`, destructured as `{ hasRecentlyViewed, recentlyViewedIds }` (Phase 1's real returned shape, read directly from `useRecentlyViewedHistory.ts`). Added `useRecentlyViewedProductFetch` import and call.

2. **Bug fix #2 (final shape)** — the `getRecommendations`/`getZoneRecommendations` effect now opens with:
   ```ts
   if (recommender === EINSTEIN_RECOMMENDERS.PDP_RECENTLY_VIEWED) {
     return;
   }
   ```
   before its existing `shouldFetch`/`zone`/`recommender` logic, so Recently-Viewed never fires either Einstein call.

3. **Bug fix #3 (final shape)** — the whole `if (recommender === EINSTEIN_RECOMMENDERS.PDP_RECENTLY_VIEWED) {...}` block now runs *before* `if (!isLoading && (!recommendations || recommendations.length < 1)) { return null; }`. The dead-check's code is byte-identical to before, just relocated; every other recommender still hits it unchanged afterward.
   - **I verified this precisely rather than trusting the task's paraphrase**: read `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-einstein.js:462-463` directly. `recommendations` initializes to `[]` (not `undefined`), so the dead-check's `!recommendations` clause is actually `false` (`[]` is truthy) — it's the `recommendations.length < 1` clause (`0 < 1`) that makes the check fire. Same practical bug, more precise mechanism; my code comments state this precisely rather than repeating the slightly imprecise "`!recommendations` will be true" framing.

4. **Bug fix #4** — inside the branch: `recentlyViewedProducts.map((product) => selectRecentlyViewedCard(product, formatPrice)).filter(...).map(...)` replaces the old `(recommendations?.recs ?? []).map(...)` chain; `<ZimmRecentlyViewedRail title={title} cards={cards} />` replaces the `title || recommendations?.displayMessage` fallback.

5. **Bug fix #5** — verified, not modified: `useEinstein()`'s `recommendations` stays `[]` for this branch (per #3's finding), so `recommendations?.recs` in the `sendViewReco`/`dataCloud.sendViewRecommendations` effect is `[].recs` → `undefined` → falsy. The effect already no-ops correctly; confirmed by direct source reading, not assumed.

6. **`ref`/`{...props}` forwarding** on the `<Box>` wrapper: untouched, exactly as it was.

7. Docblock updated in place (not rewritten): the A6 paragraph now states current behaviour; a new dated (2026-09-08) paragraph explains the three consequences of the data-source swap, following the same "state current truth + dated correction" pattern already used in `recentlyViewedCard.ts`/`useRecentlyViewedHistory.ts` rather than leaving stale text to contradict.

**`/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/overrides/app/components/recommended-products/index.test.tsx`** — full rewrite of the Recently-Viewed describe block: mocks `useRecentlyViewedHistory` and `useRecentlyViewedProductFetch` (smallest-surface, same `vi.mock` pattern as before) instead of `useRecentlyViewedGate`/reading `recommendations.recs`. Five tests: RV-renders-rail (with a real null-filtering case), the "any other recommender" `test.each` (unchanged intent, still fed by real `recommendations.recs`), RV-gate-false-renders-null, and a new dedicated **dead-check-reordering regression test**.

### Proof the regression test is real, not vacuous
Per this codebase's "prove, don't assert" standard, I temporarily reverted just the ordering (moved the dead-check back above the RV branch), ran the suite, confirmed exactly the two ordering-dependent tests failed (`TestingLibraryElementError: Unable to find an element by: [data-testid="zimm-recently-viewed-rail-stub"]`), then restored the fix and reconfirmed all tests pass. This is the "make it fail on purpose first" discipline the plan itself repeatedly invokes (finding 18).

### Verification results
- `npx tsc --noEmit` → **exit 0, project-wide clean** (this was the one file blocking it).
- `npx vitest run` on the two target files → **5/5 pass**.
- `npm run test` (full suite, including the hard styling gate) → **71 test files, 1080 tests, all pass**, including `overrides/app/theme/components/recipeGuards.test.ts` (6/6).

### Live dev-server check (http://localhost:3000, not restarted)
Homepage/PLP SSR HTML don't embed product links directly, so I found real product IDs via `/search?q=dress` (the same query the `zimmproductcard-live-demo` branch used against this sandbox): `8637DS241`, `ZWNEWPRD03`, `ZWNEWPRD04`. Curled `http://localhost:3000/product/8637DS241`:
- **HTTP 200**, zero occurrences of this app's error-boundary markers (`An error has occurred`, `Stack Trace`, `TypeError`, `Cannot read`, `Cannot destructure`) — for comparison, a garbage ID (`/product/test-product-id`) correctly produces a real `Error: Product Not Found` stack-trace page, confirming the app's error boundary does surface real exceptions when they occur, and none occurred here.
- I checked whether the `<Island hydrateOn="visible">` wrapper around all three `RecommendedProducts` usages would prevent this from meaning anything: read `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/island/index.jsx` directly — on the server, `hydrated` initialises to `true` (`useState(ssr)`), so **children fully execute and render server-side**; only client-side hydration timing is deferred. So this request did genuinely execute my modified component's code server-side, including the reordered branch.
- No rail markup (`data-testid="recently-viewed-rail"`) appeared for any of the three rails. This is **expected, not a failure**: curl carries no `sessionStorage`/`localStorage`, so `hasRecentlyViewed` is correctly `false` for a stateless request (AC 8 — no rail, no placeholder), and Einstein returns no real data for the other two rails regardless (independently confirmed project-wide: Einstein is "Not Deployed" on every real Zimmermann site — this is pre-existing, unrelated to my change, and the dead-check code path for those two rails is untouched).
- **Explicit limitation, not overclaimed**: curl cannot carry real browser storage state, so it cannot exercise the "has history → renders real cards" path at all. That requires an actual browser (visit a PDP to write history via `markProductViewed`, then reload/navigate to see the rail render with live-fetched cards) — full interactive/hydration behaviour is not provable by curl alone.

### Autonomous decisions (my call, documented, not escalated)
1. **Scoped `useRecentlyViewedProductFetch`'s `ids` argument to the Recently-Viewed recommender only** (`recommender === EINSTEIN_RECOMMENDERS.PDP_RECENTLY_VIEWED ? recentlyViewedIds : NO_RECENTLY_VIEWED_IDS`), with a new stable `NO_RECENTLY_VIEWED_IDS` module constant. Not explicitly named in the task text (which only named the Einstein calls), but required by React's rules of hooks (the hook must be called unconditionally) and is the exact mirror-image of bug fix #2: without this, every other `RecommendedProducts` instance on the same page (e.g. PDP's own "Might Also Like") would silently fire its own redundant `getProducts` call whenever the shopper already has tracked history.
